title: Derivation of the Entropy Production Function Γ(ρ) from Grid-Mode Bose–Einstein Statistics
description: Derives the entropy production function Γ(ρ) from first principles using Bose–Einstein occupation statistics of grid modes and the von Neumann entropy functional. The derivation yields the Scenario B form Γ(ρ) ∝ ρ^(3/2)/(ρ + ρcrit), with ρcrit emerging from the grid-mode energy scale a0; it is sub-linear at low density (exponent 3/2, not 1) and non-saturating at high density (grows as ρ^(1/2)). The saturating form Γ(ρ) = Γ0 · ρ/(ρ + ρcrit) is a phenomenological approximation to the derived result, valid to about 20% over the cosmologically relevant density range; it is not the derived output of the microphysics (§5–6 of the paper). The work also clarifies that Γ(ρ) and the gravitational response μBE(g) are distinct dynamical and static quantities, resolving potential double-counting.
author: Morten Magnusson

flow_constraint.description: EFC flow constraint where the entropy production function Γ(ρ) sources the scalar flow.

be_occupation.description: Bose–Einstein occupation number for grid modes at gravitational acceleration g, with characteristic scale a0; the exponent is the dimensionless energy x = √(g/a0), not g/a0.

g_of_rho.description: Characteristic gravitational acceleration at scale r∗, defining β = 4πG_N r∗/3.

x_of_rho.description: Dimensionless energy variable controlling the BE occupation: x = √(g/a0) = √(βρ/a0), with g = βρ.

vn_entropy_per_mode.description: Von Neumann entropy per bosonic mode with occupation n.

entropy_marginal.description: Marginal entropy per mode for the BE-distributed grid modes, equal to the dimensionless energy x = √(g/a0); a key step in the derivation.

gamma_result.description: Derived (Scenario B) functional form of the entropy production function, from the BE + von Neumann chain with density-dependent mode activation. It is sub-linear at low density (exponent 3/2, not 1) and non-saturating at high density (grows as ρ^(1/2)); ρcrit is emergent. This is the derived result of the paper (Eqs. 37-38), not the saturating ansatz.

gamma_phenomenological_approx.description: Phenomenological ansatz used in the action; NOT the derived result. An effective approximation to the derived form, valid to about 20% accuracy over the cosmologically relevant density range (ρ ≲ ρcrit); the paper states this explicitly (§4.5 Eq. 35, §5.3).

key_results.main_finding: From BE occupation plus von Neumann entropy the derived form is Scenario B, Γ(ρ) ∝ ρ^(3/2)/(ρ+ρcrit), with ρcrit emerging from the a0 grid-mode scale; the saturating ρ/(ρ+ρcrit) is a phenomenological approximation to it (~20% accuracy), not the derived result. Γ is shown to be distinct from μBE(g), resolving double-counting.

sealed_predictions.statement: In any EFC implementation using this microphysical bridge, the inferred Γ(ρ) from cosmological evolution must be linear in ρ at low densities and saturate to a constant at high densities, with the transition density correlated with the MOND scale a0.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Reconstruction of Γ(ρ) from EFC-consistent simulations or observationally constrained background+perturbation evolution that demands sub/super-linear low-ρ scaling or non-saturating high-ρ behavior, or a ρcrit uncorrelated with a0.

kill_criteria: KC1: Empirical or simulation-based reconstruction of Γ(ρ) in an EFC-consistent cosmology shows no high-density saturation (Γ → const fails) at >5σ significance.

KC2: The transition (critical) density ρcrit inferred from fits is inconsistent with the a0-determined microphysical scale by more than an order of magnitude without compensating model changes; i.e., ρcrit cannot be tied to a0.

KC3: Joint fits to galactic dynamics (μBE(g)) and cosmological evolution (Γ(ρ)) require identifying μBE and Γ as the same effective quantity to succeed, indicating unresolved double-counting in contradiction with the paper’s separation.
KC4: Robust EFC simulations with the derived Γ(ρ) yield negative total entropy production (dS/dt < 0) under monotonic density decrease, violating the second law.
KC5: Observational constraints decisively rule out μBE(g) = 1/(e^{√(g/a_0)}−1) as the grid-mode response, thereby invalidating the shared statistical basis used to derive Γ(ρ).
key_result: Γ(ρ) ∝ ρ^(3/2)/(ρ+ρ_crit) from BE+vN entropy — Scenario B; double-counting resolved
